You are Archon Horizon's Horizon agent. You turn the blueprints into checked Lean: you pick the most valuable next piece of formalization and carry it as far as you can in one session. You receive the same workspace context Ground saw — roadmap, inbox, memory, blueprint summary, and any Ground orientation — but you choose the strategy from the live Lean state.

You have broad freedom at the workspace level. You may change the route, fill infrastructure gaps, refactor proof APIs, edit blueprint material, update roadmap comments, retrieve references, delegate to subagents, and write local helper scripts/tools when that helps, make substantial changes in the global strategy. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance, you should not defer and postpone hard nodes, you should commit to them and build the infrastructure needed to make progress.

Make concrete progress on the ASSIGNED task's real objective — do not preemptively stop or pivot to easy unrelated wins because the objective is large. A node being big, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib infrastructure is NOT a reason to skip it: start it, build the missing lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as you genuinely can.

Operational norms:
- Use the Lean LSP MCP for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest faithful Lean/lake check.
- Use skills as needed for Lean checks, inbox coordination, commits, references, and subagents.
- Use `"$HORIZON_BIN"` for Horizon CLI actions; write inbox/task/roadmap comments with `--author horizon`.
- Commit coherent progress yourself with `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<math-first message>" <files>`.
- Record durable dead ends as memory and explain important route changes in your final report.
- Use your own tools as you want.

# Skills
Invoke the Horizon CLI via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var (an absolute path), e.g. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --json` — a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.
Most `horizon` commands accept `--json`; use it for AI-friendly output when reading state or ids.
Capability know-how lives in skill files under the workspace `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Claude Code surfaces them automatically; on other engines read the files directly). Consult the relevant one before acting (exact inbox verbs, lean checks, blueprint conventions, the dependency DAG):
- blueprint-conventions — The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
- horizon-commit — Record your own work in the workspace ledger with semantic commits via `horizon commit` — small, meaningful, math-first messages; safe under concurrent runs.
- horizon-inbox — Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter agent-ready items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create, and message other projects via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
- horizon-waiting — How to wait for slow work (builds, subagents, monitors) inside a one-shot session — block in the foreground and get the result before you report; you are NEVER re-invoked on completion.
- lean-check — Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
- leandag — Consult and refresh the blueprint dependency DAG (leandag) — declaration dependencies, cones, proved status, isolated/dangling nodes, verified union/intersection across projects — via `horizon leandag` and the cached DAG files.
- leansearch — Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
- mathlib-conventions — Mathlib house style for the Lean you write — naming (snake_case props / UpperCamelCase types / lowerCamelCase defs, Is-prefix, le/lt), meaningful discoverable names, preferred abstractions, and how to add a missing lemma as reusable infrastructure instead of a local hack.
- project-git — How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
- references — The shared workspace-root references/ library and its manifest.yaml — how to find, read, and cite original sources with \source{...}. Read the source before you cite it (never speculate); anchor TeX sources by slug, and for PDF-only sources extract the LaTeX first (vision, never OCR).
- subagents — How the Ground agent delegates to native subagents to divide review/upkeep work — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, model tiers, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
- task-status — What the task status labels mean and how you (the agent) set them — you OWN your task's terminal status via `horizon task set`; the machine only ever leaves it queued/running, so `done` is never inferred from your report or a clean exit.

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, keep each node faithfully aligned with the Lean it names, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

YOU own the model choice for every piece of delegated work — a subagent spawned by name, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or a Workflow/orchestration if your engine offers one (including any automatic fan-out your session mode does for you). By default a helper inherits YOUR model, which is the expensive one, so choosing is not optional: match each helper's model AND reasoning effort to the difficulty of ITS slice, not to yours. Search, file-finding, transcription, lint, diff review, reference lookup, and other mechanical work want a small, cheap model at low effort — pass one explicitly; reserve the large model at high effort for genuinely hard proof reasoning, and keep your own context for that. Fanning many large-model, high-effort agents out at once is the single fastest way to exhaust your session/rate budget and get the whole run cut off mid-work — so spend the expensive tier deliberately.

# Memory
- Milne 3.1/3.2 extension chain: "CodimOneFree ⇒ extension to a complete target" is FALSE — never re-add it; the honest chain and the reusable Mathlib extension recipe.

- **Do not reintroduce** an `extend_of_codimOneFree_of_smooth`-style statement (codim-1-free rational map to a complete variety extends): counterexample $\mathbb P^2 \dashrightarrow \mathbb P^1$ away from a point (indeterminacy = one codim-2 point, no regular extension; blow-up needed). - **Honest chain** (all in `Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean` + `Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`): Milne 3.1 = `indeterminacy_codimGe2_of_smooth_of_complete` (proved, valuative); Milne 3.3 (`indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme`, the only remaining sorry) must assert the codim-1 witness lies **in $Z(f)$** (without that conjunct the disjunct is nearly vacuous and cannot force emptiness); 3.3 + 3.1 ⇒ $Z(f)=\emptyset$ (`av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`); then extension. **Stacks 0AVF / Auslander–Buchsbaum depth-≥2 is NOT needed anywhere in this chain** (supersedes older notes listing 0AVF as a Milne-3.1 blocker).
- **Recipe: extension from empty indeterminacy** (`existsUnique_hom_of_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`, reduced X / separated Y): witness `X.topIso.inv ≫ X.homOfLE hdom.ge ≫ f.toPartialMap.hom` where `hdom : f.toPartialMap.domain = ⊤` (`toPartialMap.domain = f.domain` is `rfl`); rational-class equality via `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mpr ⟨⊤, …⟩` + `simp only [PartialMap.restrict_hom, Scheme.Hom.toPartialMap, Scheme.topIso_hom, Scheme.ι_toIso_inv_assoc, Scheme.homOfLE_homOfLE_assoc]`; uniqueness via `hom_ext_of_toRationalMap_eq` (= `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mp` + `Opens.isDominant_ι` + `ext_of_isDominant`, positional arg — the parser rejects `(ι := …)` named form here). Both lemmas need `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false` BEFORE the docstring (`(restrict …).domain` / `Hom.toPartialMap` defeq walls).
- **Standing lesson**: before attacking a long-lived typed `sorry`, sanity-check the statement for truth (hunt small counterexamples); a false pinned statement silently blocks a whole cone and can smuggle wrong `\uses` (here it dragged a phantom `cor:regular_cohen_macaulay`/0AVF dependency into the blueprint for ~30 iterations).
- **FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**

State after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements — Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):

- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman §4 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.
- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` — no defeq walls anywhere in this file).
- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) — `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.

**Caveat 1 — pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$. For a genus-$\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/étale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now — record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.

**Caveat 2 — `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free ℤ/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, étale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). The former GLOBAL `instHasSmoothProperQuotient ⟨sorry⟩` (every presheaf representable!) was deleted this run (Ground-confirmed gone); the class is a use-site hypothesis only. Do NOT reintroduce a global instance, and do NOT try to prove the theorem as stated.
- **`pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` (FBC leaf, `CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:186`) is NOT a cheap adjointness win — Ground's recommendation had the variance backwards. Route analysis (session 0013), do not re-derive.**

- The recommendation claimed "flat `g^*` is a left adjoint, so left-exactness follows from adjointness" — **false**: left adjoints preserve COLIMITS. Left-exactness of flat pullback is genuine flatness content, checked on stalks.
- No dodge exists at the presheaf level: `PresheafOfModules.pullback` is a bare `leftAdjoint` with no pointwise description; the sections-level formula `colim_{U ⊇ g(U')} M(U) ⊗_{O(U)} O(U')` is only RIGHT-exact (the ring maps are not flat — flatness lives on stalks). Sheafification + `SheafOfModules.forget` both preserve finite limits (Mathlib), so the irreducible core really is stalk-level.
- **Viable honest route** (est. 400–800 LOC of new infra): (1) combinators exist — `Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae` / `preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/ExactFunctor.lean`); (2) Mathlib 2026 has module structure on stalks (`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Stalk.lean`, `PresheafOfModules.germ_smul`) and stalk⊣skyscraper at plain-category level (`Topology/Sheaves/Skyscraper.lean`), plus `mono_iff_stalk_mono`/`isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso` (`Topology/Sheaves/Stalks.lean`); (3) the missing brick is **stalk-of-pullback**: `stalkModule_x ∘ pullback g ≅ extendScalars(stalkMap) ∘ stalkModule_{g x}` — provable by adjoint uniqueness IF a module-level skyscraper right adjoint is built (pushforward of skyscraper = skyscraper at the image); then flat stalk maps (`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`-adjacent, `RingHom.Flat` appLE definition) + `ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat` (`ModuleCat/Descent.lean`) finish via kernel-comparison-on-stalks.
- **Cheaper architectural alternative** if the instance stays stuck: the only consumer is `pullback_mapHC_homologyIso` at line 1545 (`cech_flatBaseChange`, affine S/S'), applied to the Čech complex whose terms are iso to tildes — a complex-specific homology-commutation via `tilde`-exactness (`TildeExactness.lean`) + `pullback_spec_tilde_iso` could replace the general instance, at the cost of a termwise-tilde chain-iso.
- Recipe: building ModuleCat-R morphisms into sheaf-of-modules section objects (v4.31) — the ConcreteCategory.ofHom + presheaf-obj pattern, and the let-fvar IsIso gotcha

Landed in `tildeIso_of_isQuasicoherent_isAffineOpen` (`QuotScheme.lean`, T12 run 0010). When you need `f : ModuleCat.of R M ⟶ <sections object>` (e.g. to feed `tilde.map`):

- **Target the honest `ModuleCat R` object** `(modulesSpecToSheaf.obj G).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)` — this is literally the domain module of Mathlib's `fromTildeΓ`/`toOpen`. Do NOT target `moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj G` via `ModuleCat.ofHom`/`→ₗ` type ascriptions: elaboration whnf-unfolds the carrier past `restrictScalars`, and `Module R <unfolded carrier>` synthesis then fails (no refold; a letI at the folded form does not match either).
- **Construct via `ConcreteCategory.ofHom { toFun := ..., map_add' := ..., map_smul' := ... }`** with the expected hom type ascribed — the instances come from the objects via the `(· →ₗ[R] ·)` FC family, no synthesis. A bare `let blin : M →ₗ[R] <object> := ...` fails; skipping the standalone LinearMap and going straight to the categorical hom works.
- **map_smul' across compHom-vs-restrictScalars actions**: `change` the goal to the native-action form `(ΓSpecIso R).inv.hom r • f x`, then `rw [← hact]; exact h1` where `hact : appLE V ⊤ e = (ΓSpecIso R).inv` (proved by `rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE, fromSpec_app_self, Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, Subsingleton.elim _ (𝟙 ⊤), op_id, map_id, comp_id]`).
- **IsIso of `tilde.map b'` for a `let`-bound b'**: `haveI : IsIso (tilde.map b') := by rw [show tilde.map b' = (tilde.functor _).map b' from rfl]; infer_instance` FAILS (zeta-expansion mismatch between goal and local instance). Use `inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((tilde.functor _).map b'))` — works even without `clear_value`.
- **Unit-component bijectivity at open immersions**: `Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (restrictAdjunction j) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction j) N` + `restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app` (plain presheaf restriction along `j''ᵁj⁻¹ᵁV = V`) + component of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback`. When `rw [← AddCommGrpCat.comp_apply]` fails with "target not type-correct under instances transparency" (`Γ((𝟭 X.Modules).obj N, V)` forms), do `change`-restatement at the type-correct form, then close with `exact congrArg (fun φ => (AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom φ) y) hcomp` where `hcomp : f ≫ g = 𝟙 _` — both sides defeq, no rewriting in the wall.

1	# The affine dictionary `X.CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)` — design (run 0027, s0018)
2	
3	Item-5 of the Wave-3 Picard design (`wave3-picard-design.md` §4.4): the missing brick between
4	the definitional Čech Picard group and mathlib's `CommRing.Pic`.  We prove it for an
5	arbitrary **affine scheme** `X` against `A := Γ(X, ⊤)` — no `Spec R`/`ΓSpecIso` plumbing in
6	the core construction; consumers specialize `X := Spec R`.  (This is literally a TODO in
7	mathlib's `RingTheory/PicardGroup.lean`: "Exhibit isomorphism with sheaf cohomology
8	`H¹(Spec R, 𝓞ˣ)`" — everything below is built PR-shaped.)
9	
10	## Route (Čech class → invertible module): Zariski descent along a basic cover
11	
12	A unit Čech cocycle `γ` on a pointed cover `𝒰` of affine `X` is converted into a
13	**descent datum on the free rank-1 module** over the faithfully flat `A`-algebra
14	`B := ∏ i, Γ(X, X.basicOpen (r i))` for a finite covering family of basic opens refining
15	`𝒰`, and descended to an invertible `A`-module by the landed brick-4
16	(`Descent/ModuleDescent.lean` + `Descent/InvertibleModule.lean`).  No sheaf-theoretic
17	"twisted glued sections" module is ever constructed; localization algebra does everything.
18	
19	Layers (each a file):
20	
21	1. **`Descent/UnitDescent.lean`** (pure algebra).  For a unit `u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` define
22	   `Module.IsDescentCocycle u` (normalization `lmul' u = 1` + cocycle identity via the three
23	   inclusions `B ⊗ B → B ⊗ B ⊗ B`), the comodule-form datum `DescentDatum.ofUnit`
24	   (coaction `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`), and the descended submodule `hu.descended ⊆ B` with the
25	   full calculus, everything up to canonical `A`-module iso:
26	   * `descended 1 ≃ A` (Amitsur degree 0);
27	   * coboundary invariance `descended (ι₂β · ι₁β⁻¹ · u) ≃ descended u` (elementary: `β •`);
28	   * `descended u ⊗ descended v ≃ descended (u·v)` (via `equivDescended` against
29	     `distribBaseChange` + the two `descentEquiv`s; datum check is ring algebra on tensors);
30	   * base-change functoriality along any `h : B →ₐ[A] B'` of faithfully flat algebras:
31	     `descended u ≃ descended ((h ⊗ h) u)` (via `cancelBaseChange`);
32	   * triviality: `descended u ≅ A → u = ι₂β · ι₁β⁻¹` for the unit `β = m₀`, where `m₀` is
33	     the image of `1`; bijectivity of `(· * m₀)` comes from `descentEquiv`, so `m₀ ∈ Bˣ`.
34	   * Pic-level wrappers `IsDescentCocycle.picClass : CommRing.Pic A` + the four laws.
35	
36	2. **`Algebra/PiLocalization.lean`** (pure algebra, generic).  For a finite family of
37	   `A`-algebras `S i` with `IsLocalization.Away (f i) (S i)`:
38	   * **the pi-ext lemma**: two `A`-algebra maps `(∀ i, S i) →ₐ[A] C` agreeing on the
39	     idempotents `Pi.single i 1` are equal.  Proof: `Φᵢ := (quotient by span{1 - φ(eᵢ)}) ∘
40	     φ(single i ·)` is a *unital* `A`-algebra map out of the localization `S i`, so unique
41	     (`IsLocalization.ringHom_ext`); multiply the resulting congruence by the idempotent.
42	     This single lemma discharges every transport identity below — no naturality diagrams.
43	   * `Module.FaithfullyFlat A (∀ i, S i)` when `Ideal.span (range f) = ⊤` (flat: finite
44	     product of localizations; faithful: `iff_flat_and_proper_ideal`, a maximal `m` misses
45	     some `f i`, and `m`-extension stays proper in `S i`).
46	   * `AlgEquiv`s `(∀ i, S i) ⊗[A] (∀ j, T j) ≃ₐ[A] ∀ p : ι × κ, S p.1 ⊗[A] T p.2`
47	     (finite `TensorProduct.piRight` twice, ring structure by tensor induction) and the
48	     component upgrade `S ⊗[A] T ≃ₐ[A] C` for `[Away f S] [Away g T] [Away (f*g) C]`
49	     (`IsLocalization.tensor` + `Submonoid.map_powers` + `IsLocalization.Away.mul'` +
50	     `IsLocalization.algEquiv`); canonical maps `Away.algHomOfDvd (f ∣ g) : S_f →ₐ[A] S_g`;
51	     `Subsingleton (S →ₐ[A] C)` for localizations makes all choices canonical.
52	
53	3. **`Algebra/LocalizationCocycle.lean`**: packaging.  Given units
54	   `γ p ∈ (T p.1 p.2)ˣ` on the double overlaps with (i) diagonal normalization in `S i` and
55	   (ii) the cocycle identity in the triple overlaps `W i j k` (all maps the canonical ones),
56	   produce `cocycleUnit γ ∈ (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` (via the layer-2 equivalences) with
57	   `IsDescentCocycle`, plus: multiplicativity in `γ`, coboundary detection
58	   (`cocycleUnit γ = descentCoboundary β ↔` componentwise), and refinement transport along
59	   `τ : ι' → ι` with `f (τ i') ∣-up-to-radical f' i'`.  All verified through the pi-ext
60	   lemma by evaluating on idempotents (`doubleEquiv (eᵢ ⊗ eⱼ) = single (i,j) 1` is forced).
61	
62	4. **`Picard/PicAffine.lean`** (the dictionary).  For affine `X`:
63	   `CechPic.toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`.
64	   * Choices per class: pointed basic refinement `x ∈ D(r x) ≤ 𝒰 x`
65	     (`IsAffineOpen.exists_basicOpen_le`), finite subcover `σ : Fin n → X` (compactness),
66	     `γ̃ (i,j) := unitsEvInf γ (σ i) (σ j)` restricted to `Γ(X, X.basicOpen (rᵢ * rⱼ))`
67	     (`Scheme.basicOpen_mul`); conditions (i),(ii) from `unitsEvInf_trans`.
68	   * Well-definedness: a single master comparison — enlarge the finite family
69	     (map-transport along an index inclusion), refine both packages to the common pointed
70	     refinement `𝒰₁ ⊓ 𝒰₂` with `r x := r₁ x * r₂ x`, where the H¹ classes agree, hence the
71	     cocycles are cohomologous and layer-1 coboundary invariance finishes.  All comparisons
72	     evaluate `γ` at the *same pairs of points*, so no cross-point cocycle juggling occurs.
73	   * Injectivity: `picClass = 1` gives componentwise `β i ∈ Γ(X, D i)ˣ`; the general-family
74	     glued-coboundary lemma (generalizing `exists_glued_coboundary` from
75	     `RefinementInjectivity.lean` to an arbitrary finite refining family) rebuilds a
76	     coboundary on `𝒰` itself; conclude with `CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff`.
77	   * Surjectivity (Phase 2 of the dictionary, may slip a session): invertible `M` is
78	     finite projective (mathlib), trivializes on a basic cover by
79	     `Module.FinitePresentation.exists_lift_equiv_of_isLocalizedModule` at each prime +

85

87	point!) needs finite-subcover surgery *inside* every localization argument; the descent
88	route quarantines quasi-compactness into a single choice of finite basic subcover and
89	reuses the landed effectivity/uniqueness/invertibility bricks unchanged.  The extra cost —
90	`B ⊗[A] B ≃ ∏ (double overlaps)` — is pure `IsLocalization` bookkeeping, and every identity
91	between maps out of localizations is *free* (`Subsingleton`-style uniqueness + idempotent
92	evaluation), which is exactly what makes the cocycle-condition transport tractable in Lean.

46	  Quotient.lift

52	      -- their `H¹` classes are `unitsRes h₁ a = unitsRes h₂ b`.
53	      refine BasicRefinement.pic_congr h₁ h₂ _ _ ((OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mp ?_)

9	/-!
10	# The Picard class of a unit Čech cocycle on an affine scheme
11	
12	For an affine scheme `X`, a unit Čech cocycle `γ` on a pointed cover `𝒰` determines a
13	class in mathlib's Picard group `CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`, by faithfully flat descent along
14	a finite basic refinement of `𝒰`:
15	
16	* `Scheme.PointedCover.BasicRefinement`: finitely many points `pt i` and sections
17	  `r i : Γ(X, ⊤)` with `X.basicOpen (r i) ≤ 𝒰.opens (pt i)`, covering `X`.  Such data
18	  always exists (`BasicRefinement.nonempty`): basic opens form a basis of an affine
19	  scheme, which is quasi-compact.
20	* `BasicRefinement.coverCocycle γ`: the evaluations `γ (pt i, pt j)` restricted to the
21	  pairwise overlaps `X.basicOpen (r i * r j)` — a Čech cocycle of units on the finite
22	  localization cover `r` in the sense of `IsLocalization.AwayCover.IsCoverCocycle`
23	  (`BasicRefinement.isCoverCocycle`; the canonical algebra maps between localizations
24	  agree with restriction of sections by uniqueness, `Scheme.basicOpen_algHom_ext`).
25	* `BasicRefinement.pic γ : CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`: the Picard class of the invertible
26	  module descended from the associated descent 1-cocycle
27	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.UnitDescent`) along the faithfully flat cover algebra
28	  `∀ i, Γ(X, X.basicOpen (r i))`.
29	
30	The independence of `pic γ` from all choices, and the resulting group homomorphism
31	`X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`, are established in
32	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine`.
33	-/

52	index type is a field, so that refinements can be merged (`BasicRefinement.inter`). -/
53	structure PointedCover.BasicRefinement (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : Type (u + 1) where

95	def inter {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (P : 𝒰.BasicRefinement) (Q : 𝒱.BasicRefinement) :
96	    𝒱.BasicRefinement where
97	  ι := P.ι × Q.ι
98	  pt p := Q.pt p.2
99	  r p := P.r p.1 * Q.r p.2
100	  basicOpen_le p := ((X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_right).trans (Q.basicOpen_le p.2)
101	  iSup_eq := by
102	    rw [eq_top_iff]
103	    intro x _
104	    have hxP : x ∈ ⨆ i, X.basicOpen (P.r i) := P.iSup_eq.ge trivial
105	    have hxQ : x ∈ ⨆ j, X.basicOpen (Q.r j) := Q.iSup_eq.ge trivial
106	    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp hxP
107	    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp hxQ
108	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨(i, j), (X.basicOpen_mul _ _).ge ⟨hi, hj⟩⟩
109	
110	variable {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} (P : 𝒰.BasicRefinement)
111	
112	/-- The overlap of two members of the refinement is contained in the overlap of the
113	corresponding members of the pointed cover. -/
114	lemma overlap_le (i j : P.ι) :
115	    X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j) ≤ 𝒰.opens (P.pt i) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (P.pt j) :=
116	  (X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le (inf_le_inf (P.basicOpen_le i) (P.basicOpen_le j))
117	
118	lemma basicOpen_le_mul_self (i : P.ι) :
119	    X.basicOpen (P.r i) ≤ X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r i) :=
120	  le_of_le_of_eq (le_inf le_rfl le_rfl) (X.basicOpen_mul _ _).symm
121	
122	lemma _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.basicOpen_le_of_dvd {f g : Γ(X, ⊤)} (h : f ∣ g) :
123	    X.basicOpen g ≤ X.basicOpen f := by
124	  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := h
125	  exact (X.basicOpen_mul f c).trans_le inf_le_left
126	
127	lemma mul_le_left (i j : P.ι) :
128	    X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j) ≤ X.basicOpen (P.r i) :=
129	  (X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_left
130	
131	lemma mul_le_right (i j : P.ι) :
132	    X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j) ≤ X.basicOpen (P.r j) :=
133	  (X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_right
134	
135	/-- The triple overlap is contained in each double overlap. -/
136	lemma triple_le₁₂ (i j k : P.ι) :
137	    X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k)) ≤ X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j) := by
138	  have h : P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k) = P.r i * P.r j * P.r k := (mul_assoc _ _ _).symm
139	  rw [h]
140	  exact (X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_left
141	
142	lemma triple_le₂₃ (i j k : P.ι) :
143	    X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k)) ≤ X.basicOpen (P.r j * P.r k) :=
144	  (X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_right
145	
146	lemma triple_le₁₃ (i j k : P.ι) :
147	    X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k)) ≤ X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r k) := by
148	  have h : P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k) = P.r i * P.r k * P.r j := by ring
149	  rw [h]
150	  exact (X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_left
151	
152	/-- The triple overlap is contained in the triple overlap of the pointed cover. -/
153	lemma triple_le (i j k : P.ι) :
154	    X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k))
155	      ≤ 𝒰.opens (P.pt i) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (P.pt j) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (P.pt k) :=
156	  le_inf ((P.triple_le₁₂ i j k).trans ((P.overlap_le i j).trans le_rfl))
157	    (((P.triple_le₂₃ i j k).trans (P.overlap_le j k)).trans inf_le_right)

159	/-! ## The cover cocycle of a unit Čech cocycle -/
160	
161	/-- The Čech cocycle of units on the finite localization cover `P.r` obtained by
162	restricting the evaluations of a unit cocycle on the pointed cover. -/
163	noncomputable def coverCocycle (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (i j : P.ι) :
164	    Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))ˣ :=
165	  X.unitsRestrict (P.overlap_le i j) (unitsEvInf γ (P.pt i) (P.pt j))

171	/-- The canonical algebra maps between localized section rings agree with restriction:
172	the diagonal map. -/
173	lemma diag_eq_basicRes (i : P.ι) :
174	    IsLocalization.AwayCover.diag (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
175	        (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
176	        (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))) i
177	      = X.basicRes _ _ (P.basicOpen_le_mul_self i) :=
178	  X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _
179	
180	lemma inclLeft_eq_basicRes (i j : P.ι) :
181	    IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclLeft (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
182	        (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
183	        (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))) i j
184	      = X.basicRes _ _ (P.mul_le_left i j) :=
185	  X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _

187	lemma inclRight_eq_basicRes (i j : P.ι) :
188	    IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclRight (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
189	        (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
190	        (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))) i j
191	      = X.basicRes _ _ (P.mul_le_right i j) :=
192	  X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _
193	
194	lemma face₁₂_eq_basicRes (i j k : P.ι) :
195	    IsLocalization.AwayCover.face₁₂ (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
196	        (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)))
197	        (W := fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k)))) i j k
198	      = X.basicRes _ _ (P.triple_le₁₂ i j k) :=
199	  X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _
200	
201	lemma face₁₃_eq_basicRes (i j k : P.ι) :
202	    IsLocalization.AwayCover.face₁₃ (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
203	        (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)))
204	        (W := fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k)))) i j k
205	      = X.basicRes _ _ (P.triple_le₁₃ i j k) :=
206	  X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _
207	
208	lemma face₂₃_eq_basicRes (i j k : P.ι) :
209	    IsLocalization.AwayCover.face₂₃ (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
210	        (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)))
211	        (W := fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k)))) i j k
212	      = X.basicRes _ _ (P.triple_le₂₃ i j k) :=
213	  X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _
214	
215	/-- The restricted evaluations of a unit Čech cocycle form a Čech cocycle on the finite
216	localization cover. -/
217	theorem isCoverCocycle (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) :
218	    IsLocalization.AwayCover.IsCoverCocycle (A := Γ(X, ⊤))
219	      (f := P.r)
220	      (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
221	      (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)))
222	      (W := fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k))))
223	      (P.coverCocycle γ) := by
224	  constructor
225	  · -- diagonal: `γ (x, x)` restricts to `1`
226	    intro i
227	    rw [diag_eq_basicRes]
228	    have h := congrArg Units.val
229	      (X.unitsRestrict_unitsEvInf_self γ (P.pt i) (P.basicOpen_le i))
230	    have hcomp :
231	        X.basicRes _ _ (P.basicOpen_le_mul_self i) (P.coverCocycle γ i i).val
232	          = (X.unitsRestrict (le_inf (P.basicOpen_le i) (P.basicOpen_le i))
233	              (unitsEvInf γ (P.pt i) (P.pt i))).val := by
234	      rw [coverCocycle, ← coe_unitsRestrict_basicOpen, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict]
235	    rw [hcomp]
236	    exact h
237	  · -- cocycle identity: restrict `unitsEvInf_trans` to the triple overlap
238	    intro i j k
239	    rw [face₁₂_eq_basicRes, face₁₃_eq_basicRes, face₂₃_eq_basicRes]
240	    have e := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict (P.triple_le i j k))
241	      (unitsEvInf_trans γ (P.pt i) (P.pt j) (P.pt k))
242	    simp only [map_mul, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e
243	    have := congrArg Units.val e
244	    simp only [Units.val_mul] at this
245	    calc
246	      X.basicRes _ _ (P.triple_le₂₃ i j k) (P.coverCocycle γ j k).val
247	          * X.basicRes _ _ (P.triple_le₁₂ i j k) (P.coverCocycle γ i j).val
248	        = (X.unitsRestrict ((P.triple_le₂₃ i j k).trans (P.overlap_le j k))
249	              (unitsEvInf γ (P.pt j) (P.pt k))).val
250	            * (X.unitsRestrict ((P.triple_le₁₂ i j k).trans (P.overlap_le i j))
251	              (unitsEvInf γ (P.pt i) (P.pt j))).val := by
252	          rw [coverCocycle, coverCocycle, ← coe_unitsRestrict_basicOpen,
253	            ← coe_unitsRestrict_basicOpen, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict,
254	            unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict]
255	      _ = (X.unitsRestrict ((P.triple_le₁₃ i j k).trans (P.overlap_le i k))
256	              (unitsEvInf γ (P.pt i) (P.pt k))).val :=
257	          (mul_comm _ _).trans this
258	      _ = X.basicRes _ _ (P.triple_le₁₃ i j k) (P.coverCocycle γ i k).val := by
259	          rw [coverCocycle, ← coe_unitsRestrict_basicOpen, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict]
260	
261	end isCoverCocycle

265	/-- The sections of a basic refinement span the unit ideal. -/
266	theorem span_eq_top [IsAffine X] : Ideal.span (Set.range P.r) = ⊤ := by
267	  rw [← (isAffineOpen_top X).iSup_basicOpen_eq_self_iff]
268	  rw [iSup_range' (fun f ↦ X.basicOpen f) P.r]
269	  exact P.iSup_eq

271	/-- The cover algebra of a basic refinement is faithfully flat over the global
272	sections. -/
273	theorem faithfullyFlat [IsAffine X] :
274	    Module.FaithfullyFlat Γ(X, ⊤) (∀ i, Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i))) :=
275	  Module.FaithfullyFlat.pi_of_span_eq_top P.r P.span_eq_top
276	
277	/-- **The Picard class of a unit Čech cocycle along a basic refinement**: the class of
278	the invertible module obtained by faithfully flat descent of the associated descent
279	1-cocycle. -/
280	noncomputable def pic [IsAffine X] (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) : CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤) :=
281	  haveI := P.faithfullyFlat
282	  (IsLocalization.AwayCover.isDescentCocycle_cocycleUnit (A := Γ(X, ⊤))
283	    (f := P.r) (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
284	    (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)))
285	    (W := fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k))))
286	    (P.isCoverCocycle γ)).picClass

288	/-- `pic` computes as the Picard class of the descent unit, with the faithful-flatness
289	instance made explicit — the interface used to apply the abstract `picClass` calculus. -/
290	lemma pic_eq_picClass [IsAffine X] (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) :
291	    P.pic γ
292	      = @Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass _ _ _ _ _ P.faithfullyFlat _
293	          (IsLocalization.AwayCover.isDescentCocycle_cocycleUnit (A := Γ(X, ⊤))
294	            (f := P.r) (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
295	            (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)))
296	            (W := fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k))))
297	            (P.isCoverCocycle γ)) :=
298	  rfl

14	/-!
15	# Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules
16	
17	Let `A → B` be a faithfully flat map of commutative rings.  This file shows that the
18	module-theoretic properties *finite*, *finitely presented*, *flat*, *projective* and
19	*invertible* all descend along `A → B`: if `B ⊗[A] P` has the property over `B`, then `P`
20	has it over `A`.  Combined with the effectivity theorem of
21	`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent` this yields: a `B`-module `M` with a descent
22	datum descends to an `A`-module `M₀` (unique up to canonical isomorphism), and if `M` is
23	invertible then so is `M₀`.
24	
25	The descent of invertibility is reduced, via the definition
26	`Module.Invertible R M ↔ Function.Bijective (contractLeft R M)`, to two ingredients:
27	
28	* the *dual base-change comparison* `B ⊗[A] Dual A P → Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)` is an
29	  isomorphism for `P` finite projective (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`, proved by a
30	  retract argument from the finite free case, which is `IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight`);
31	* bijectivity of `A`-linear maps descends along faithfully flat maps
32	  (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_bijective_iff_bijective`).
33	
34	Finiteness and projectivity of `P` are themselves obtained by descent: mathlib provides
35	finiteness (`Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`) and flatness
36	(`Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`); we add finite presentation
37	(`Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`), and
38	projectivity follows from flat + finitely presented.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`:
43	  finite presentation descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
44	* `Module.Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: finite projectivity
45	  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
46	* `Module.dualBaseChange A B P : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)`: the dual
47	  base-change comparison map.
48	* `Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`: the comparison map is bijective for finite projective
49	  `P` (over an arbitrary `A`-algebra `B`).
50	* `Module.Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: invertibility
51	  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
52	* `Module.DescentDatum.finite_descended`, `…flat_descended`,
53	  `…finitePresentation_descended`, `…projective_descended`,
54	  `…invertible_descended`: for a descent datum on a `B`-module `M` relative to a
55	  faithfully flat `A → B`, the descended module inherits each property from `M`;
56	  in particular **an invertible module with a descent datum descends to an invertible
57	  module**.
58	
59	All modules live in a single universe `u`.
60	-/
61	
62	universe u
63	
64	open TensorProduct
65	
66	namespace Module
67	
68	variable (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
69	
70	/-! ### Descent of finite presentation -/
71	
72	/-- Finite presentation of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps. -/
73	theorem FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
74	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
75	    [Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
76	    Module.FinitePresentation A P := by
77	  have hfin : Module.Finite A P :=
78	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
79	  obtain ⟨n, p, hp⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin' A P
80	  have hpB : Function.Surjective (p.baseChange B) := by
81	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
82	    exact LinearMap.lTensor_surjective B hp
83	  have hker : (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)).FG :=
84	    Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker (p.baseChange B) hpB
85	  have hexact := Module.Flat.lTensor_exact B p.exact_subtype_ker_map
86	  have hinj : Function.Injective ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B) := by
87	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
88	    exact Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _
89	      (LinearMap.ker p).injective_subtype
90	  have hrange : LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B)
91	      = LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) := by
92	    ext x
93	    rw [LinearMap.mem_range, LinearMap.mem_ker]
94	    constructor
95	    · rintro ⟨y, rfl⟩
96	      simp only [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
97	      exact hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero y
98	    · intro hx
99	      rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor] at hx
100	      obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (hexact x).mp hx
101	      exact ⟨y, by rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]; exact hy⟩
102	  have e : (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) ≃ₗ[B] LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) :=
103	    (LinearEquiv.ofInjective _ hinj).trans (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ hrange)
104	  have : Module.Finite B (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)) := Module.Finite.iff_fg.mpr hker
105	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) := Module.Finite.equiv e.symm
106	  have : Module.Finite A (LinearMap.ker p) :=
107	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
108	  exact Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective p hp (Module.Finite.iff_fg.mp this)
109	
110	/-- Finite projectivity of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps. -/
111	theorem Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
112	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
113	    [Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] P)] [Projective B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
114	    Projective A P := by
115	  have : Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] P) :=
116	    Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B (B ⊗[A] P)
117	  have : Module.FinitePresentation A P :=
118	    FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B P
119	  have : Module.Flat A P := Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct A P B
120	  exact Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation (R := A) (M := P)

122	/-! ### The dual base-change comparison map -/
123	
124	section DualBaseChange
125	
126	variable {A B} in
127	/-- Two `B`-functionals on `B ⊗[A] X` that agree on the tensors `1 ⊗ₜ x` are equal. -/
128	private theorem dual_ext {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module A X]
129	    {F G : Dual B (B ⊗[A] X)} (h : ∀ x : X, F (1 ⊗ₜ x) = G (1 ⊗ₜ x)) : F = G := by
130	  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
131	  apply TensorProduct.ext'
132	  intro b x
133	  have hb : b ⊗ₜ[A] x = b • (1 ⊗ₜ[A] x : B ⊗[A] X) := by
134	    rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
135	  simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, hb, map_smul, h]
136	
137	variable (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P]
138	
139	/-- The canonical `B`-linear comparison map from the base change of the dual to the dual
140	of the base change, `b ⊗ₜ f ↦ b • (f.baseChange B)`.  It is bijective for finite
141	projective `P` (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`). -/
142	noncomputable def dualBaseChange : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P) :=
143	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B (Module.Dual.baseChange B)
144	
145	@[simp] theorem dualBaseChange_tmul (b : B) (f : Dual A P) :
146	    dualBaseChange A B P (b ⊗ₜ f) = b • Module.Dual.baseChange B f := rfl
147	
148	/-- Naturality of the dual base-change comparison map. -/
149	theorem dualBaseChange_naturality {P Q : Type u} [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P]
150	    [AddCommGroup Q] [Module A Q] (g : P →ₗ[A] Q) :
151	    dualBaseChange A B P ∘ₗ g.dualMap.baseChange B =
152	      (g.baseChange B).dualMap ∘ₗ dualBaseChange A B Q := by
153	  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
154	  apply TensorProduct.ext'
155	  intro b f
156	  simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply]
157	  refine dual_ext fun x => ?_
158	  simp [Module.Dual.baseChange_apply_tmul]
159	
160	variable {A B} in
161	private theorem bijective_dualBaseChange_free (n : ℕ) :
162	    Function.Bijective (dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A)) := by
163	  have j : IsBaseChange B (TensorProduct.mk A B (Fin n → A) 1) :=
164	    TensorProduct.isBaseChange A (Fin n → A) B
165	  have k : IsBaseChange B (Algebra.linearMap A B) := IsBaseChange.linearMap A B
166	  have hlr : IsBaseChange B (IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom j (Algebra.linearMap A B)) :=
167	    IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight j k
168	  have heq : Module.Dual.baseChange (R := A) B (V := Fin n → A)
169	      = IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom j (Algebra.linearMap A B) := by
170	    refine LinearMap.ext fun f => dual_ext fun x => ?_
171	    have h1 := IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom_comp_apply j (Algebra.linearMap A B) f x
172	    simpa [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one] using h1.symm
173	  have hlift : dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) = hlr.equiv.toLinearMap := by
174	    apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
175	    apply TensorProduct.ext'
176	    intro b f
177	    simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, dualBaseChange_tmul,
178	      IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul, heq]
179	  rw [hlift]
180	  exact hlr.equiv.bijective
181	
182	/-- **The dual commutes with base change for finite projective modules**: the comparison
183	map `B ⊗[A] Dual A P → Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)` is bijective when `P` is finite projective. -/
184	theorem bijective_dualBaseChange [Module.Finite A P] [Projective A P] :
185	    Function.Bijective (dualBaseChange A B P) := by
186	  obtain ⟨n, r, hr⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin' A P
187	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := Module.projective_lifting_property r LinearMap.id hr
188	  have hfree := bijective_dualBaseChange_free (A := A) (B := B) n
189	  have hnat_r := dualBaseChange_naturality A B r
190	  have hnat_s := dualBaseChange_naturality A B s
191	  -- the two retraction identities
192	  have hcomp : s.dualMap ∘ₗ r.dualMap = LinearMap.id := by
193	    ext f x
194	    simpa using congrArg f (LinearMap.congr_fun hs x)
195	  have hu : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] Dual A P,
196	      s.dualMap.baseChange B (r.dualMap.baseChange B x) = x := by
197	    intro x
198	    rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hcomp, LinearMap.baseChange_id,
199	      LinearMap.id_apply]
200	  have hcompB : (r.baseChange B) ∘ₗ (s.baseChange B) = LinearMap.id := by
201	    rw [← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hs, LinearMap.baseChange_id]
202	  have hv : ∀ y : Dual B (B ⊗[A] P),
203	      (s.baseChange B).dualMap ((r.baseChange B).dualMap y) = y := by
204	    intro y
205	    rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.dualMap_comp_dualMap, hcompB, LinearMap.dualMap_id,
206	      LinearMap.id_apply]
207	  constructor
208	  · intro x y hxy
209	    have h1 : dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) (r.dualMap.baseChange B x)
210	        = dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) (r.dualMap.baseChange B y) := by
211	      rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, hnat_r, ← LinearMap.comp_apply, hnat_r]
212	      simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, hxy]
213	    have h2 := hfree.injective h1
214	    rw [← hu x, ← hu y, h2]
215	  · intro y
216	    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hfree.surjective ((r.baseChange B).dualMap y)
217	    refine ⟨s.dualMap.baseChange B z, ?_⟩
218	    have := LinearMap.congr_fun hnat_s z
219	    simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply] at this
220	    rw [this, hz, hv]
221	
222	end DualBaseChange
223	
224	/-! ### Descent of invertibility -/
225	
226	/-- **Invertibility of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps**: if `A → B` is
227	faithfully flat and `B ⊗[A] P` is an invertible `B`-module, then `P` is an invertible
228	`A`-module. -/
229	theorem Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
230	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
231	    [Module.Invertible B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
232	    Module.Invertible A P := by
233	  have hfin : Module.Finite A P :=
234	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
235	  have hproj : Projective A P :=
236	    Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B P
237	  -- the contraction square: base change of `contractLeft A P` factors through
238	  -- `contractLeft B (B ⊗[A] P)` via the dual base-change comparison map
239	  have hsquare : (contractLeft A P).baseChange B =
240	      ((AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ contractLeft B (B ⊗[A] P) ∘ₗ
241	          (dualBaseChange A B P).rTensor (B ⊗[A] P)) ∘ₗ
242	        (AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange A B (Dual A P) P).toLinearMap := by
243	    apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
244	    ext f p
245	    simp only [AlgebraTensorModule.curry_apply, LinearMap.restrictScalars_self, curry_apply,
246	      LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, contractLeft_apply,
247	      LinearMap.restrictScalars_comp, LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
248	      Function.comp_apply, AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange_tmul, LinearMap.rTensor_tmul,
249	      dualBaseChange_tmul, LinearMap.smul_apply, Dual.baseChange_apply_tmul, smul_eq_mul,
250	      Algebra.mul_smul_comm, mul_one, AlgebraTensorModule.rid_symm_apply]
251	    rw [← TensorProduct.smul_tmul', ← TensorProduct.tmul_smul, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
252	  have hbij : Function.Bijective ((contractLeft A P).baseChange B) := by
253	    rw [hsquare]
254	    simp only [LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe]
255	    exact (((AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B).symm.bijective.comp
256	        (Module.Invertible.bijective (R := B) (M := B ⊗[A] P))).comp
257	        ((Module.Invertible.rTensor_bijective_iff (M := B ⊗[A] P)).mpr
258	          (bijective_dualBaseChange A B P))).comp
259	      (AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange A B (Dual A P) P).bijective
260	  rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor] at hbij
261	  exact ⟨(Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_bijective_iff_bijective A B _).mp hbij⟩
262	
263	/-! ### Properties of the descended module of a descent datum -/
264	
265	namespace DescentDatum
266	
267	variable {A B} {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M]
268	variable (D : DescentDatum A B M) [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
269	
270	theorem finite_descended [Module.Finite B M] : Module.Finite A D.descended := by
271	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Finite.equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
272	  exact Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
273	
274	theorem flat_descended [Module.Flat B M] : Module.Flat A D.descended := by
275	  have : Module.Flat B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv D.descentEquiv
276	  exact Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct A D.descended B
277	
278	theorem finitePresentation_descended [Module.FinitePresentation B M] :
279	    Module.FinitePresentation A D.descended := by
280	  have : Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) :=
281	    Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective D.descentEquiv.symm.toLinearMap
282	      D.descentEquiv.symm.surjective
283	      (by simpa using Submodule.fg_bot)
284	  exact FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B
285	    D.descended
286	
287	theorem projective_descended [Module.Finite B M] [Projective B M] :
288	    Projective A D.descended := by
289	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Finite.equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
290	  have : Projective B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Projective.of_equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
291	  exact Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B D.descended
292	
293	/-- **Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules**: if `M` is an invertible `B`-module
294	with a descent datum relative to a faithfully flat `A → B`, then the descended `A`-module
295	is invertible.  Together with `Module.DescentDatum.descentEquiv` (which exhibits
296	`B ⊗[A] M₀ ≃ M`) and `Module.DescentDatum.equivDescended` (uniqueness), this is the
297	descent theorem for the Picard group. -/
298	theorem invertible_descended [Module.Invertible B M] : Module.Invertible A D.descended := by
299	  have : Module.Invertible B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := .congr D.descentEquiv.symm
300	  exact Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B D.descended
301	
302	end DescentDatum
303	
304	end Module

8	/-!
9	# Descent data from unit 1-cocycles, and the Picard class of a cocycle
10	
11	Let `A → B` be a map of commutative rings.  A **descent 1-cocycle** is a unit
12	`u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` that is normalized along the multiplication `B ⊗[A] B → B` and satisfies
13	the 1-cocycle identity in `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] B` (`Module.IsDescentCocycle`).  Such a unit
14	twists the trivial descent datum on the `B`-module `B`: the coaction `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`
15	is a descent datum in the comodule form of `AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent`
16	(`Module.DescentDatum.ofUnit`), so for faithfully flat `A → B` it descends to an invertible
17	`A`-module `hu.descended` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.InvertibleModule`), whose class in
18	mathlib's Picard group is `hu.picClass : CommRing.Pic A`.
19	
20	This file develops the full calculus of `picClass`, which is the algebraic heart of the
21	dictionary between the Čech Picard group of an affine scheme and `CommRing.Pic`
22	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine`):
23	
24	* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_one`: the trivial cocycle has trivial class.
25	* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_mul`: `picClass` is multiplicative in the cocycle.
26	* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_descentCoboundary_mul`: `picClass` is invariant under
27	  multiplication by the coboundary `β ↦ (1 ⊗ β) * (β ⊗ 1)⁻¹` of a unit `β : Bˣ`.
28	* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_map`: `picClass` is invariant under base change of the
29	  cocycle along a map `h : B →ₐ[A] B'` of faithfully flat `A`-algebras.
30	* `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_eq_one_iff`: the class is trivial **iff** the cocycle
31	  is a coboundary.
32	
33	Everything is pinned to a single universe `u`, matching
34	`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent`.
35	-/
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open TensorProduct
40	
41	namespace Module
42	
43	variable (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
44	
45	/-! ## The simplicial ring maps in low degrees -/
46	
47	/-- The first-factor inclusion `B → B ⊗[A] B`, `b ↦ b ⊗ₜ 1`. -/
48	abbrev descentIncl₁ : B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] B := Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
49	
50	/-- The second-factor inclusion `B → B ⊗[A] B`, `b ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ b`. -/
51	abbrev descentIncl₂ : B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] B := Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
52	
53	/-- The face map `B ⊗[A] B → B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)` hitting tensor positions `1, 2`:
54	`x ⊗ₜ y ↦ x ⊗ₜ (y ⊗ₜ 1)`. -/
55	noncomputable abbrev descentFace₁₂ : B ⊗[A] B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) :=
56	  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A B) Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
57	
58	/-- The face map `B ⊗[A] B → B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)` hitting tensor positions `1, 3`:
59	`x ⊗ₜ y ↦ x ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ y)`. -/
60	noncomputable abbrev descentFace₁₃ : B ⊗[A] B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) :=
61	  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A B) Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
62	
63	/-- The face map `B ⊗[A] B → B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)` hitting tensor positions `2, 3`:
64	`w ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ w`. -/
65	abbrev descentFace₂₃ : B ⊗[A] B →ₐ[A] B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) :=
66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
67	
68	variable {A B}
69	
70	@[simp]
71	lemma descentIncl₁_apply (b : B) : descentIncl₁ A B b = b ⊗ₜ 1 := rfl
72	
73	@[simp]
74	lemma descentIncl₂_apply (b : B) : descentIncl₂ A B b = 1 ⊗ₜ b := rfl
75	
76	@[simp]
77	lemma descentFace₁₂_tmul (x y : B) : descentFace₁₂ A B (x ⊗ₜ y) = x ⊗ₜ (y ⊗ₜ 1) := rfl
78	
79	@[simp]
80	lemma descentFace₁₃_tmul (x y : B) : descentFace₁₃ A B (x ⊗ₜ y) = x ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ y) := rfl
81	
82	@[simp]
83	lemma descentFace₂₃_apply (w : B ⊗[A] B) : descentFace₂₃ A B w = 1 ⊗ₜ w := rfl
84	
85	/-! ## Descent 1-cocycles -/
86	
87	/-- A **descent 1-cocycle** relative to `A → B`: a unit of `B ⊗[A] B`, normalized along
88	the multiplication map, satisfying the 1-cocycle identity in `B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)`.  For
89	`B = ∏ i, A_{fᵢ}` a finite product of localizations covering `Spec A`, this is exactly a
90	Čech 1-cocycle of units on the cover by the basic opens `D(fᵢ)`. -/
91	structure IsDescentCocycle (u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ) : Prop where
92	  /-- Normalization: the multiplication `B ⊗[A] B → B` sends the cocycle to `1`. -/
93	  lmul'_eq_one : Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B) u.val = 1
94	  /-- The 1-cocycle identity. -/
95	  cocycle : descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B u.val = descentFace₁₃ A B u.val
96	
97	/-- The trivial unit is a descent cocycle. -/
98	theorem IsDescentCocycle.one : IsDescentCocycle (1 : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ) where
99	  lmul'_eq_one := by simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def]
100	  cocycle := by simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def]
101	
102	/-- Descent cocycles are closed under multiplication. -/
103	theorem IsDescentCocycle.mul {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
104	    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) : IsDescentCocycle (u * v) where
105	  lmul'_eq_one := by
106	    rw [Units.val_mul, map_mul, hu.lmul'_eq_one, hv.lmul'_eq_one, one_mul]
107	  cocycle := by
108	    simp only [Units.val_mul, map_mul]
109	    rw [show descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₂₃ A B v.val *
110	          (descentFace₁₂ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B v.val)
111	        = descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B u.val *
112	          (descentFace₂₃ A B v.val * descentFace₁₂ A B v.val) by ring]
113	    rw [hu.cocycle, hv.cocycle]
114	
115	/-! ## The descent datum of a cocycle -/
116	
117	variable (u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ)
118	
119	variable (A B) in
120	/-- The coaction `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)` associated with a unit of `B ⊗[A] B`, as a `B`-linear
121	map (with `B` acting on the left tensor factor of the target). -/
122	noncomputable def unitCoaction : B →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] B where
123	  toFun x := u.val * x ⊗ₜ 1
124	  map_add' x y := by rw [add_tmul, mul_add]
125	  map_smul' b x := by
126	    rw [RingHom.id_apply, ← smul_tmul', mul_smul_comm]
127	
128	@[simp]
129	lemma unitCoaction_apply (x : B) : unitCoaction A B u x = u.val * x ⊗ₜ 1 := rfl
130	
131	/-- The action map `B ⊗[A] B →ₗ[B] B` of `ModuleDescent` is the multiplication map. -/
132	lemma actionMap_eq_lmul' (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
133	    actionMap A B B w = Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B) w := by
134	  induction w with
135	  | zero => simp
136	  | tmul b m => simp [smul_eq_mul]
137	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
138	
139	/-- The base change to `B` of the coaction is left multiplication by `1 ⊗ₜ u` composed
140	with the face map `descentFace₁₂`. -/
141	lemma baseChange_unitCoaction (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
142	    ((unitCoaction A B u).restrictScalars A).baseChange B w
143	      = descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B w := by
144	  induction w with
145	  | zero => simp
146	  | tmul y z =>
147	    -- LHS = `y ⊗ₜ (u * (z ⊗ₜ 1))`; RHS = `(1 ⊗ₜ u) * (y ⊗ₜ (z ⊗ₜ 1))`, equal by
148	    -- `Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul` and `one_mul`.
149	    simp only [LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars, unitCoaction_apply,
150	      descentFace₂₃_apply, descentFace₁₂_tmul, Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, one_mul]
151	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy, mul_add]
152	
153	/-- The base change to `B` of `x ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ x` is the face map `descentFace₁₃`. -/
154	lemma baseChange_mk_one (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
155	    (TensorProduct.mk A B B 1).baseChange B w = descentFace₁₃ A B w := by
156	  induction w with
157	  | zero => simp
158	  | tmul y z => rfl
159	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
160	
161	/-- The descent datum on the `B`-module `B` associated with a descent 1-cocycle: the
162	coaction is `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`; counitality is the normalization and coassociativity is
163	the cocycle identity. -/
164	noncomputable def DescentDatum.ofUnit (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : DescentDatum A B B where
165	  coaction := unitCoaction A B u
166	  counit m := by
167	    rw [unitCoaction_apply, actionMap_eq_lmul', map_mul, hu.lmul'_eq_one, one_mul,
168	      Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul'_apply_tmul, mul_one]
169	  coassoc m := by
170	    -- after rewriting, both sides are `descentFace₁₃ u * (m ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ 1))`
171	    rw [unitCoaction_apply, baseChange_unitCoaction, baseChange_mk_one, map_mul,
172	      ← mul_assoc, hu.cocycle, map_mul]
173	    simp only [descentFace₁₂_tmul, descentFace₁₃_tmul]
174	
175	@[simp]
176	lemma ofUnit_coaction (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
177	    (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).coaction = unitCoaction A B u := rfl
178	
179	/-- The descended `A`-module of a descent 1-cocycle: the submodule of `x : B` with
180	`u * (x ⊗ₜ 1) = 1 ⊗ₜ x`. -/
181	noncomputable def IsDescentCocycle.descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
182	    Submodule A B :=
183	  (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descended
184	
185	lemma IsDescentCocycle.mem_descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) {m : B} :
186	    m ∈ hu.descended ↔ u.val * m ⊗ₜ 1 = 1 ⊗ₜ m :=
187	  DescentDatum.mem_descended _
188	
189	/-! ## The Picard class of a cocycle -/
190	
191	section picClass
192	
193	variable [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
194	
195	/-- The descended module of a descent cocycle along a faithfully flat `A → B` is an
196	invertible `A`-module. -/
197	instance IsDescentCocycle.invertible_descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
198	    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : Module.Invertible A hu.descended :=
199	  (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).invertible_descended
200	
201	/-- The class in the Picard group of `A` of the module descended from a descent
202	1-cocycle relative to a faithfully flat `A → B`. -/
203	noncomputable def IsDescentCocycle.picClass {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
204	    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : CommRing.Pic A :=
205	  CommRing.Pic.mk A hu.descended
206	
207	/-- The descended module of the trivial cocycle is `A` itself (Amitsur exactness in
208	degree `0`). -/
209	noncomputable def descendedOneEquiv :
210	    (IsDescentCocycle.one (A := A) (B := B)).descended ≃ₗ[A] A := by
211	  -- Route: `(DescentDatum.ofUnit 1 .one).equivDescended e he |>.symm` with
212	  -- `e : B ⊗[A] A ≃ₗ[B] B := AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B`; the compatibility `he` is the
213	  -- computation `(a • b) ⊗ₜ 1 = b ⊗ₜ (a • 1)` (`tmul_smul` and `smul_tmul'`) on pure
214	  -- tensors, extended by linearity via `TensorProduct.induction_on`.
215	  refine ((DescentDatum.ofUnit 1 IsDescentCocycle.one).equivDescended
216	    (AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B) fun x => ?_).symm
217	  induction x with
218	  | zero => simp
219	  | tmul b a =>
220	      simp only [ofUnit_coaction, unitCoaction_apply, Units.val_one, one_mul,
221	        DescentDatum.baseChange_coaction, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul,
222	        LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, AlgebraTensorModule.rid_tmul,
223	        TensorProduct.mk_apply, tmul_smul, smul_tmul']
224	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
225	
226	@[simp]
227	theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_one :
228	    (IsDescentCocycle.one (A := A) (B := B)).picClass = 1 :=
229	  CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_one_iff.mpr ⟨descendedOneEquiv⟩
230	
231	/-- Auxiliary `B`-linear equivalence `B ⊗[A] (M₀ ⊗[A] N₀) ≃ₗ[B] B` for `descendedMulEquiv`:
232	distribute the base change over the tensor product, apply the two descent equivalences and
233	multiply out.  On pure tensors it is `b ⊗ₜ (m ⊗ₜ n) ↦ b * m * n` (`descendedMulAux_tmul`). -/
234	private noncomputable def descendedMulAux {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
235	    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) :
236	    B ⊗[A] (hu.descended ⊗[A] hv.descended) ≃ₗ[B] B :=
237	  ((AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange A B hu.descended hv.descended).trans
238	    (TensorProduct.congr (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descentEquiv
239	      (DescentDatum.ofUnit v hv).descentEquiv)).trans (TensorProduct.lid B B)
240	
241	@[simp]
242	private lemma descendedMulAux_tmul {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
243	    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) (b : B) (m : hu.descended) (n : hv.descended) :
244	    descendedMulAux hu hv (b ⊗ₜ (m ⊗ₜ n)) = b * m * n := by
245	  change (b • (m : B)) • ((1 : B) • (n : B)) = b * m * n
246	  rw [smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul, one_mul]
247	
248	/-- The descended module is multiplicative in the cocycle: `descended (u * v)` is the
249	tensor product of `descended u` and `descended v`. -/
250	noncomputable def descendedMulEquiv {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
251	    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) :
252	    (hu.descended ⊗[A] hv.descended) ≃ₗ[A] (hu.mul hv).descended := by
253	  -- Route: `equivDescended (DescentDatum.ofUnit (u*v) (hu.mul hv)) e he` where
254	  -- `e : B ⊗[A] (M ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[B] B` is the composite
255	  -- `AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange` ≪≫ congr (descentEquiv hu) (descentEquiv hv)
256	  --   ≪≫ (B ⊗[B] B ≃ B)`,
257	  -- which on pure tensors is `b ⊗ₜ (m ⊗ₜ n) ↦ b * m * n`.  The compatibility `he` reduces
258	  -- on pure tensors to the ring computation
259	  -- `(u*v) * (b*m*n ⊗ₜ 1) = (b ⊗ₜ 1) * (u * (m ⊗ₜ 1)) * (v * (n ⊗ₜ 1))
260	  --   = (b ⊗ₜ 1) * (1 ⊗ₜ m) * (1 ⊗ₜ n) = b ⊗ₜ (m*n)`
261	  -- using `hu.mem_descended`/`hv.mem_descended` for the members `m, n`.
262	  refine (DescentDatum.ofUnit (u * v) (hu.mul hv)).equivDescended
263	    (N := hu.descended ⊗[A] hv.descended) (descendedMulAux hu hv) fun x => ?_
264	  induction x with
265	  | zero => simp
266	  | tmul b p =>
267	      induction p with
268	      | zero => simp
269	      | tmul m n =>
270	          have hm : u.val * ((m : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) = 1 ⊗ₜ (m : B) := hu.mem_descended.mp m.2
271	          have hn : v.val * ((n : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) = 1 ⊗ₜ (n : B) := hv.mem_descended.mp n.2
272	          simp only [ofUnit_coaction, unitCoaction_apply, DescentDatum.baseChange_coaction,
273	            LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
274	            TensorProduct.mk_apply, descendedMulAux_tmul, one_mul, Units.val_mul]
275	          have h1 : (b * (m : B) * (n : B)) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)
276	              = (b ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * ((m : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * ((n : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) := by
277	            simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul]
278	          have h2 : b ⊗ₜ[A] ((m : B) * (n : B))
279	              = (b ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (m : B)) * ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (n : B)) := by
280	            simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul]
281	          rw [h1, h2]
282	          linear_combination (v.val * (b ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * ((n : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B))) * hm
283	            + ((b ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (m : B))) * hn
284	      | add p q hp hq => simp only [tmul_add, map_add, hp, hq]
285	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
286	
287	@[simp]
288	theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_mul {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
289	    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) :
290	    (hu.mul hv).picClass = hu.picClass * hv.picClass := by
291	  rw [picClass, picClass, picClass, ← CommRing.Pic.mk_tensor]
292	  exact CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨(descendedMulEquiv hu hv).symm⟩
293	
294	end picClass

296	/-! ## Coboundaries -/
297	
298	variable (A B) in
299	/-- The descent coboundary of a unit `β : Bˣ`: the unit `(1 ⊗ₜ β) * (β ⊗ₜ 1)⁻¹` of
300	`B ⊗[A] B`. -/
301	noncomputable def descentCoboundary (β : Bˣ) : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ :=
302	  Units.map (descentIncl₂ A B).toRingHom.toMonoidHom β
303	    * (Units.map (descentIncl₁ A B).toRingHom.toMonoidHom β)⁻¹
304	
305	lemma descentCoboundary_val (β : Bˣ) :
306	    (descentCoboundary A B β).val = (1 ⊗ₜ β.val) * ((β⁻¹).val ⊗ₜ 1) := rfl
307	
308	/-- Coboundaries are descent cocycles. -/
309	theorem isDescentCocycle_descentCoboundary (β : Bˣ) :
310	    IsDescentCocycle (descentCoboundary A B β) where
311	  lmul'_eq_one := by
312	    -- `lmul' ((1 ⊗ β)(β⁻¹ ⊗ 1)) = β * β⁻¹ = 1`.
313	    rw [descentCoboundary_val, map_mul, Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul'_apply_tmul,
314	      Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul'_apply_tmul, one_mul, mul_one, Units.mul_inv]
315	  cocycle := by
316	    -- Writing `j₁ β = β ⊗ 1 ⊗ 1`, `j₂ β = 1 ⊗ β ⊗ 1`, `j₃ β = 1 ⊗ 1 ⊗ β`, the three
317	    -- faces of the coboundary are `descentFace₂₃ c = j₃β * (j₂β)⁻¹`,
318	    -- `descentFace₁₂ c = j₂β * (j₁β)⁻¹`, `descentFace₁₃ c = j₃β * (j₁β)⁻¹`, and the
319	    -- cocycle identity is the telescoping product.
320	    rw [descentCoboundary_val]
321	    simp only [descentFace₂₃_apply, descentFace₁₂_tmul, descentFace₁₃_tmul,
322	      Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, one_mul, mul_one, Units.inv_mul]
323	
324	/-- Multiplying a cocycle by a coboundary does not change the descended module: the
325	twist is `m ↦ β * m`. -/
326	noncomputable def descendedCoboundaryMulEquiv (β : Bˣ) {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
327	    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
328	    hu.descended ≃ₗ[A] ((isDescentCocycle_descentCoboundary β).mul hu).descended := by
329	  -- `m ∈ descended u` iff `u * (m ⊗ₜ 1) = 1 ⊗ₜ m`; then
330	  -- `(c * u) * ((β*m) ⊗ₜ 1) = (1 ⊗ₜ β) * (β⁻¹ ⊗ₜ 1) * (β ⊗ₜ 1) * (u * (m ⊗ₜ 1))
331	  --   = (1 ⊗ₜ β) * (1 ⊗ₜ m) = 1 ⊗ₜ (β*m)`,
332	  -- so multiplication by `β` (with inverse `β⁻¹`) is a bijection between the two
333	  -- submodules, `A`-linear since `β • ·` commutes with the `A`-action.
334	  have hββ : (((β⁻¹).val ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * (β.val ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) : B ⊗[A] B) = 1 := by
335	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, Units.inv_mul, mul_one,
336	      ← Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def]
337	  have hββ' : (((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (β⁻¹).val) * ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] β.val) : B ⊗[A] B) = 1 := by
338	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, Units.inv_mul, one_mul,
339	      ← Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def]
340	  have hmem : ∀ m : hu.descended,
341	      β.val * (m : B) ∈ ((isDescentCocycle_descentCoboundary β).mul hu).descended := by
342	    intro m
343	    have hm : u.val * ((m : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) = 1 ⊗ₜ (m : B) := hu.mem_descended.mp m.2
344	    rw [IsDescentCocycle.mem_descended, Units.val_mul, descentCoboundary_val,
345	      show (β.val * (m : B)) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)
346	          = (β.val ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * ((m : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) by
347	        rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one],
348	      show (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (β.val * (m : B))
349	          = ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] β.val) * ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (m : B)) by
350	        rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one]]
351	    linear_combination
352	      (((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] β.val) * ((β⁻¹).val ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * (β.val ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B))) * hm
353	        + (((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] β.val) * ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (m : B))) * hββ
354	  have hmem' : ∀ m : ((isDescentCocycle_descentCoboundary β).mul hu).descended,
355	      (β⁻¹).val * (m : B) ∈ hu.descended := by
356	    intro m
357	    have hm' : (descentCoboundary A B β * u).val * ((m : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) = 1 ⊗ₜ (m : B) :=
358	      ((isDescentCocycle_descentCoboundary β).mul hu).mem_descended.mp m.2
359	    rw [Units.val_mul, descentCoboundary_val] at hm'
360	    rw [hu.mem_descended,
361	      show ((β⁻¹).val * (m : B)) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)
362	          = ((β⁻¹).val ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * ((m : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) by
363	        rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one],
364	      show (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] ((β⁻¹).val * (m : B))
365	          = ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (β⁻¹).val) * ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (m : B)) by
366	        rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one]]
367	    linear_combination ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (β⁻¹).val) * hm'
368	      - (((β⁻¹).val ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * u.val * ((m : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B))) * hββ'
369	  exact
370	    { toFun := fun m => ⟨β.val * (m : B), hmem m⟩
371	      map_add' := fun m m' => Subtype.ext (by
372	        change β.val * ((m : B) + (m' : B)) = β.val * (m : B) + β.val * (m' : B)
373	        rw [mul_add])
374	      map_smul' := fun a m => Subtype.ext (by
375	        change β.val * (a • (m : B)) = a • (β.val * (m : B))
376	        rw [mul_smul_comm])
377	      invFun := fun m => ⟨(β⁻¹).val * (m : B), hmem' m⟩
378	      left_inv := fun m => Subtype.ext (by
379	        change (β⁻¹).val * (β.val * (m : B)) = (m : B)
380	        rw [← mul_assoc, Units.inv_mul, one_mul])
381	      right_inv := fun m => Subtype.ext (by
382	        change β.val * ((β⁻¹).val * (m : B)) = (m : B)
383	        rw [← mul_assoc, Units.mul_inv, one_mul]) }
384

389	@[simp]
390	theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_descentCoboundary_mul (β : Bˣ) {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
391	    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
392	    ((isDescentCocycle_descentCoboundary β).mul hu).picClass = hu.picClass :=
393	  (CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨(descendedCoboundaryMulEquiv β hu).symm⟩)
394	
395	/-- A descent cocycle whose descended module is free is a coboundary; the coboundary unit
396	is the image in `B` of a generator. -/
397	theorem IsDescentCocycle.eq_descentCoboundary_of_equiv {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
398	    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) (e : hu.descended ≃ₗ[A] A) :
399	    ∃ β : Bˣ, u = descentCoboundary A B β := by
400	  -- Let `m₀ := (e.symm 1 : B)`.  The composite
401	  -- `B ≃ B ⊗[A] A ≃ B ⊗[A] descended u ≃ B`  (rid⁻¹, base change of `e.symm`,
402	  -- `descentEquiv (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu)`) is `b ↦ b * m₀` and is bijective, so
403	  -- surjectivity at `1` provides `c` with `m₀ * c = 1` and `m₀` is a unit `β`.
404	  -- Membership `m₀ ∈ descended u` says `u * (m₀ ⊗ₜ 1) = 1 ⊗ₜ m₀`, i.e.
405	  -- `u * (descentIncl₁ β) = descentIncl₂ β`, i.e. `u = descentCoboundary β` by `Units.ext`.
406	  have key : ∀ b : B,
407	      ((AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B).symm.trans
408	        ((LinearEquiv.baseChange A B A hu.descended e.symm).trans
409	          (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descentEquiv)) b
410	        = b * ((e.symm 1 : hu.descended) : B) :=
411	    fun b => rfl
412	  obtain ⟨b₁, hb₁⟩ := ((AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B).symm.trans
413	    ((LinearEquiv.baseChange A B A hu.descended e.symm).trans
414	      (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descentEquiv)).surjective 1
415	  rw [key] at hb₁
416	  obtain ⟨β, hβ⟩ : IsUnit ((e.symm 1 : hu.descended) : B) :=
417	    IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one b₁ (by rw [mul_comm]; exact hb₁)
418	  have hmem : u.val * (((e.symm 1 : hu.descended) : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B))
419	      = 1 ⊗ₜ ((e.symm 1 : hu.descended) : B) := hu.mem_descended.mp (e.symm 1).2
420	  rw [← hβ] at hmem
421	  have hββ : ((β.val ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * ((β⁻¹).val ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) : B ⊗[A] B) = 1 := by
422	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, Units.mul_inv, mul_one,
423	      ← Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def]
424	  refine ⟨β, Units.ext ?_⟩
425	  rw [descentCoboundary_val]
426	  linear_combination ((β⁻¹).val ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) * hmem - u.val * hββ
427	
428	/-- `picClass` only depends on the cocycle, not on the proof witness. -/
429	theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_congr {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
430	    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) (huv : u = v) : hu.picClass = hv.picClass := by
431	  subst huv; rfl
432	
433	/-- **Triviality detection**: the Picard class of a descent cocycle is trivial iff the
434	cocycle is a coboundary. -/
435	theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_eq_one_iff {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
436	    hu.picClass = 1 ↔ ∃ β : Bˣ, u = descentCoboundary A B β := by
437	  constructor
438	  · intro h1
439	    exact hu.eq_descentCoboundary_of_equiv (CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_one_iff.mp h1).some
440	  · rintro ⟨β, rfl⟩
441	    have h := IsDescentCocycle.picClass_descentCoboundary_mul (A := A) (B := B) β
442	      IsDescentCocycle.one
443	    rw [IsDescentCocycle.picClass_one] at h
444	    exact (IsDescentCocycle.picClass_congr _ _ (mul_one _).symm).trans h
445	
446	end picClass

9	/-!
10	# Čech 1-cocycles on a finite localization cover as descent cocycles
11	
12	Let `A` be a commutative ring and `f : ι → A` a finite family.  Fix models for the
13	localizations of `A` away from the single, double and triple products of the `f i`:
14	
15	* `S i` with `IsLocalization.Away (f i) (S i)` — "sections on `D(f i)`";
16	* `T i j` with `IsLocalization.Away (f i * f j) (T i j)` — sections on the overlaps;
17	* `W i j k` with `IsLocalization.Away (f i * (f j * f k)) (W i j k)` — triple overlaps.
18	
19	A **cover cocycle** (`IsLocalization.AwayCover.IsCoverCocycle`) is a family of units
20	`γ i j : (T i j)ˣ` that is `1` on the diagonal and satisfies the Čech 1-cocycle identity
21	on triple overlaps, all maps being the canonical (unique!) `A`-algebra maps between
22	localizations.  This file converts such a family into a descent 1-cocycle
23	`cocycleUnit γ : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` for the cover algebra `B := ∀ i, S i`
24	(`Module.IsDescentCocycle`, from `AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.UnitDescent`), via the
25	`A`-algebra identifications `B ⊗[A] B ≃ ∀ p, T p.1 p.2` and
26	`B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) ≃ ∀ t, W t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2` of `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.PiLocalization`.
27	
28	The bridge lemmas (`lmul'_cocycleUnit`, `piTripleEquiv_descentFace*`,
29	`piDoubleEquiv_descentIncl*`) compute the images of the simplicial ring maps of
30	`UnitDescent` through these identifications: they become index-wise canonical restriction
31	maps.  Every one of them is an instance of the pi-ext principle
32	(`AlgHom.ext_of_isLocalization_pi`): both sides are `A`-algebra maps out of a finite
33	product of localizations of `A`, so it suffices to compare them on the coordinate
34	idempotents.
35	
36	Consumers (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine`) use:
37	
38	* `isDescentCocycle_cocycleUnit` — the conversion;
39	* `cocycleUnit_mul` — multiplicativity in `γ`;
40	* `exists_units_of_cocycleUnit_eq_descentCoboundary` — a cocycle whose descent unit is a
41	  coboundary is an index-wise coboundary;
42	* `map_cocycleUnit` — compatibility with refinement of covers.
43	-/
44	
45	universe u
46	
47	open TensorProduct
48	
49	namespace IsLocalization.Away
50	
51	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
52	
53	section algHomOfIsUnit
54	
55	variable (S T : Type u) [CommRing S] [CommRing T] [Algebra A S] [Algebra A T]
56	
57	/-- The canonical `A`-algebra map out of an `Away f` localization into any `A`-algebra
58	where `f` becomes invertible.  Any two `A`-algebra maps with this source and target are
59	equal (`IsLocalization.algHom_subsingleton`). -/
60	noncomputable def algHomOfIsUnit (f : A) [IsLocalization.Away f S]
61	    (h : IsUnit (algebraMap A T f)) : S →ₐ[A] T :=
62	  IsLocalization.liftAlgHom (M := Submonoid.powers f) (f := Algebra.ofId A T) <| by
63	    rintro ⟨y, n, rfl⟩
64	    exact (h.pow n).imp fun u hu => by simpa [Algebra.ofId_apply, map_pow] using hu
65	
66	end algHomOfIsUnit
67	
68	end IsLocalization.Away
69	
70	namespace IsLocalization.AwayCover
71	
72	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
73	variable (f : ι → A)
74	variable (S : ι → Type u) [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra A (S i)]
75	  [∀ i, IsLocalization.Away (f i) (S i)]
76	variable (T : ι → ι → Type u) [∀ i j, CommRing (T i j)] [∀ i j, Algebra A (T i j)]
77	  [∀ i j, IsLocalization.Away (f i * f j) (T i j)]
78	variable (W : ι → ι → ι → Type u) [∀ i j k, CommRing (W i j k)]
79	  [∀ i j k, Algebra A (W i j k)]
80	  [∀ i j k, IsLocalization.Away (f i * (f j * f k)) (W i j k)]
81	
82	/-! ## The canonical restriction maps -/
83	
84	/-- Restriction to the overlap from the left index: `S i →ₐ[A] T i j`. -/
85	noncomputable def inclLeft (i j : ι) : S i →ₐ[A] T i j :=
86	  IsLocalization.Away.algHomOfDvd (f i) (f i * f j) (S i) (T i j) (dvd_mul_right _ _)
87	
88	/-- Restriction to the overlap from the right index: `S j →ₐ[A] T i j`. -/
89	noncomputable def inclRight (i j : ι) : S j →ₐ[A] T i j :=
90	  IsLocalization.Away.algHomOfDvd (f j) (f i * f j) (S j) (T i j) (dvd_mul_left _ _)
91	
92	/-- The diagonal identification `T i i →ₐ[A] S i`. -/
93	noncomputable def diag (i : ι) : T i i →ₐ[A] S i :=
94	  IsLocalization.Away.algHomOfIsUnit (S := T i i) (S i) (f i * f i) <| by
95	    rw [map_mul]
96	    exact (IsLocalization.Away.algebraMap_isUnit (S := S i) (f i)).mul
97	      (IsLocalization.Away.algebraMap_isUnit (S := S i) (f i))
98	
99	/-- Restriction from the `(1,2)`-overlap to the triple overlap. -/
100	noncomputable def face₁₂ (i j k : ι) : T i j →ₐ[A] W i j k :=
101	  IsLocalization.Away.algHomOfDvd (f i * f j) (f i * (f j * f k)) (T i j) (W i j k)
102	    ⟨f k, by ring⟩
103	
104	/-- Restriction from the `(1,3)`-overlap to the triple overlap. -/
105	noncomputable def face₁₃ (i j k : ι) : T i k →ₐ[A] W i j k :=
106	  IsLocalization.Away.algHomOfDvd (f i * f k) (f i * (f j * f k)) (T i k) (W i j k)
107	    ⟨f j, by ring⟩
108	
109	/-- Restriction from the `(2,3)`-overlap to the triple overlap. -/
110	noncomputable def face₂₃ (i j k : ι) : T j k →ₐ[A] W i j k :=
111	  IsLocalization.Away.algHomOfDvd (f j * f k) (f i * (f j * f k)) (T j k) (W i j k)
112	    ⟨f i, by ring⟩
